chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti who said:
He was asked about the speckled crow, so he said: 'It is not eaten.' He said: 'And who permitted you to eat the black one?'

key_terms.الْأَسْوَدَ: The black one (referring to the black crow)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating speckled versus black crows according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (AS) distinguishes between the speckled crow (*al-ghurab al-abqa'*), which is deemed impermissible, and the black crow, which is permitted, addressing a specific juristic nuance regarding avian consumption. The questioner’s follow-up highlights the logical consistency of the Imam’s ruling, clarifying that the prohibition is not universal to all crows but specific to the speckled variety, thereby resolving potential confusion in dietary laws. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise categorization (*takhassus*) in fiqh, where physical characteristics can dictate legal status.
